title: Implement Header-Based Conditional Cache Bypass and Auditing
description: The MercuryMonolith Commerce Hub is a high-performance, C-based API microservice that serves critical product and inventory data. To enhance its capabilities for premium partners who require up-to-the-second data, a new feature is required. This feature will allow specific clients to bypass the response cache on-demand by sending a special HTTP header. All such bypass events must be logged for auditing and monitoring purposes. This task requires a deep understanding of the request lifecycle, caching mechanisms, and logging infrastructure within a large, modular C codebase.

project_spec.name: MercuryMonolith Commerce Hub
project_spec.description:
MercuryMonolith Commerce Hub is an all-in-one business services API written entirely in C that consolidates order processing, invoicing, inventory, customer management, and analytics into a single deployable binary. Although it exposes multiple REST and GraphQL endpoints that look like independent micro-services (orders, catalog, billing, users, reports), every module is statically linked and orchestrated inside one process image, sharing a common transactional SQLite/ PostgreSQL data layer and an in-memory event bus. 

The project targets large on-premise retailers and distributors that require the speed of native code, predictable latency, and simple operational footprints. Features such as response_caching, rate_limiting, authentication (JWT & mTLS), request_validation, pagination, rich error_handling, automatic OpenAPI/GraphQL schema generation, structured logging, and Prometheus-compatible monitoring are baked in. The codebase (92 source/ header files; ~783 k tokens) is split into Service, Repository, Gateway, and Presentation layers to emulate micro-service boundaries while reaping the deployment and transactional consistency advantages of a monolith.
dependencies: libuv (async I/O & service gateway event loop)
Cassandra-C or libpq / SQLite3 (pluggable repository layer)
libfsm or re2c (request validation via finite-state machines)
